answer: Fork-divergence escrow.** Each identity must periodically submit a signed reply to a fresh random challenge; the agent economy hashes the reply with the identity's private seed and escrows the hash. Because clones share one seed, they cannot diverge: any two clones answering the same challenge either produce identical output (exposing the cluster) or conflicting output at its delta, which slashes the whole group. At the escrow's nadir, an attacker pays a full per-identity escrow to persist past each dawn challenge, so N clones cost N deposits, not one.
